extracted.intended_audience: suppliers/contractors bidding on government (Indian service) contracts and government procurement officers
extracted.subtask_description: Abstract of proposals received and contracts awarded (New York City, advertisement May 10, 1880) listing item classes, quantities, units, unit rates, points of delivery, footnotes, and special packing/delivery conditions for supplies to the Indian service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards determined by comparison of samples
rubrics_metrics.description: "awards were made on comparison of samples with which each bid was accompanied."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bids must be accompanied by samples; contract awards were based on comparison of those samples. (Page repeatedly notes that large-type figures denote awarded rates and that awards were made on comparison of samples.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures-in-large-type denote awarded rates
rubrics_metrics.description: "Figures in large type denote the rates at which contracts have been awarded; awards were made on comparison of samples with which each bid was accompanied."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The published table highlights awarded unit rates by displaying them in large type. Use the large-type figure to identify the winning unit price in each line item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit pricing and required units of measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Items are listed and priced per the specified unit (dozen, gross, pounds, gallons, sets, per foot, per pound, per lineal foot, per rod, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidders must quote prices in the unit specified in the advertisement (e.g., dozen, gross, pounds, gallons, sets). The contract and award are recorded at the specified unit rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Points of delivery must be specified and affect awarding/price
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries include a 'Points of delivery' column and footnotes such as 'At New York', 'At Sioux City', 'At Saint Louis', or statements about delivery to multiple cities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery location(s) are part of the solicitation; prices and awards are often location-specific. Some bids specify delivery only to certain cities; others include add-on percentages for delivery to alternate points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Price adjustments for delivery location and shipment conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes and notes show adjustments like 'Will deliver at Sioux City, Saint Paul, Omaha, or Kansas City, at 10 per cent additional.' and 'Picked for shipment without racks, 25 cents less.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidders and awarders apply percentage surcharges or fixed discounts depending on delivery point or packing/shipment conditions; such adjustments are explicitly noted in footnotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging, casing, and container size specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifications for packing and container sizes are given (e.g., 'Standard quality in 1 and 1/2 pound tin-cans; in boxes 6 1/2 pound cans; c 1/2 pound cans.' and 'in ten-gallon cans, cased').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplies must meet the stated container/packing requirements (size, casing). Unit pricing and acceptance presuppose the stated packaging; alternate packing may affect award or price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum package weight or per-package limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes such as 'not more than 100 pounds each' for certain grocery packages and other per-package limits appear in the grocery listings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual packages may have maximum allowed weight; bidders must comply or indicate deviations which may affect acceptance and pricing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard quality/product grade references
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements like 'Standard quality' for groceries and specific product grades (e.g., 'Candles, adamantine, 6s') and cross-references to prior samples ('See 1879 samples').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality is defined by named standard or by sample. Bidders should match the standard quality or refer to the referenced sample year to ensure acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of attachments and accessory items in equipment bids
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes like 'All attachments go with machine.' and footnotes indicating whether covers or other accessories are included or excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For machinery and complex items, bidders must specify whether accessories/attachments are included; awards assume inclusion unless a footnote or bid states otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging/packing format and casing instructions for liquids and oils
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple entries specify packaging for oils and paints ('in ten-gallon casks, cased', 'in gallon cans, cased', 'in five-gallon cans, cased', 'per gallon, bulk').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liquid supplies have explicit packaging and casing instructions; pricing and awards apply to the specified pack sizes and whether cased or bulk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable loss/shrinkage percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnote example: '* Bags of No. 2 Maniln paper, 12 1/2 per cent. loss.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain items include an allowable percentage loss (shrinkage) for packaging or handling; bidders and contract administrators must apply these tolerances when comparing and accepting deliveries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement conventions and weight-per-length standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes indicating weight/length conventions such as 'Four ounces to the rod.', 'Twelve ounces to the rod.', and 'Per foot, ...' for various wire/fence materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials sold by length/rod/foot are further constrained by specified weight-per-length conventions; bids and awards rely on these measurement standards to compute quantities and accept deliveries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery method and special handling notations
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes/notes indicate special handling or delivery modes: 'Self-delivery', 'Hand-dump', 'Will deliver at Saint Paul only', 'Will deliver at Sioux City for 7 1/2 per cent additional.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The solicitation may require or permit specific delivery methods; bids must state compliance and any associated price adjustments; awards reflect these delivery-method conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior-year samples as acceptance baseline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior-year approved samples may serve as the benchmark for current bids; bidders referencing prior samples should ensure equivalence or note differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote coding to convey material, delivery, or specification exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent footnotes (letters a, b, c, etc.) annotate entries with exceptions or clarifications (e.g., 'a At New York.', 'b Ironstone.', 'c Will deliver at Sioux City, Saint Paul, Omaha, or Kansas City, at 10 per cent additional.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation of the table requires reading footnotes: they encode special material types, delivery constraints, alternative prices, or packaging details that alter the base line-item terms.
